Residential buildings account for a significant amount of the national energy use, and yet only 15 percent of them consume less than 200 kilowatt hours of electricity per year. The Burlington Free Will Community Medical Center in Massachusetts makes this a top priority by requiring all staff members to install low-errancy devices across their office areas and building general lighting.
“Without the use of these systems, our healthcare providers, our engineers, our technicians – the backbone of the insurance companies, the Nursing Homes, Children’s Programs – at least 615 hospitals, and about 1,400 nursing homes in the United States had to self-fund lighting.” Michael J. Friedenberg, Chief Vice President of Electrical Services and Interventions
There are important elements our billing experts and facility management personnel must consider, however, when helping lead your healthcare community in this endeavor.
We are talking about:
- What are you looking for?
- What materials are best for the job

unverified.cover_text:
Residential buildings account for a significant amount of the national budget and annually spend into the billions; the scale of the problem that has not been properly addressed includes congestion, the waste of unnecessary resources and waste of indivisible demand for water, gas and electricity, as well as historic urban centre consolidation. On this basis there have been recommendations in the last 5 years to have a green growth strategy embodied in the local theme and be brought to the forefront of planning strategies.
During my visit to Czechia I had the chance to meet with Cristina Sikorska and her team to find out about the way in which the long-standing relationship between sustainable city planning and parks and recreational spaces has been supported by the government. Particular attention will be given to scoring results both on the buildings and benches that are the focal points of the environment, whether in public spaces in Bucharest or Plzeň.
The Pedigree Lecture is a series of one hour public lectures designed for professionals and anyone involved in the field of urban synthesis who wishes to better
